title: Souther adequacy report
description: How well a model's `example`s cover it. Emitted by `souther examples --format json`. A reader keys on `schemaVersion`: a change that removes or renames anything here raises it, and a key added since does not — such a key is optional, so a document written before it existed is still a document of this version. That is one direction: every object here is closed, so an older copy of this schema refuses a document carrying a key added since. A reader that has to accept newer documents wants the newer schema, not a higher number.

compilerVersion.description: The compiler that produced the report, or `unreleased` when it ran from class files.

status.description: The weakest status among the modules. `partial` means something could not be read, so an absent number is not evidence of a gap.

adequacy.description: Whether the rows meet what the asked measures require, which is not what `status` says. `undetermined` is a measure that was not asked for or could not be made; a build that gates on this refuses `not_satisfied` and nothing else.

status.description: Whether a measure has a number. `unavailable` says only that it has none; the `reason` beside it says why, and the two are not read off one another.

implementation.description: `injected` is a behavior with no `let` yet; its rows are recorded rather than evaluated.

rows.description: How many example rows name this behavior, across every source that writes one.

pending.description: How many of those rows are recorded rather than evaluated.

branch.description: Which arms of the behavior's body the rows go through. Branch-arm coverage, not path coverage: going through both arms of two nested conditions says nothing about their combinations.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `no_body` is a behavior that has no arms to measure at all — a `>->` composition or one with no `let` — rather than arms nothing measured; `not_asked` is a build that did not ask for them; `unreadable` is a run whose instrumentation could not be tied back to the body; `no_rows` is a behavior no row names.

partition.description: How much of what the model distinguishes about this behavior's inputs the rows reach.

path.description: The input position, as a parameter and the fields read off it. A newtype's `value` is never a step.

classes.description: The classes a row can be written at: what the model divides this position into, less what the body declares unreachable.

excluded.description: Classes the body answers `unreachable` for. Out of `classes` because a row naming one would reach the `unreachable` and be refused, and named here because the type still has them.

reasons.description: The reasons written at the `unreachable`s this class leads to — one, unless several paths abort for different reasons.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. A behavior no row names was not measured here, so the classes nothing sits in are not classes nothing reaches.

origin.description: The rule that drew this line — a type's invariant, or a guard.

knownWritable.description: Whether some row could carry this value. False where a rule reaching the value this position sits in was not read in full — a pattern, a disequality, a strict bound on a decimal — so the edge is where the reading stopped rather than where the model does. Such a line is reported and not counted, and no build is refused over it.

reason.description: Why there is no answer, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `arms_not_asked` and `arms_unreadable` belong to a guard's line only, which is met by reaching the comparison rather than by writing the value; an invariant's line is met by writing it and is never waiting on the arms.

pairs.description: Two-class combinations across two positions. Counts rather than a ratio: a combination no row reaches has not been shown unreachable, only untried, so the denominator is not known.

witnessedFeasible.description: Combinations proven reachable, each by a row that sits in it.

provenInfeasible.description: Combinations shown impossible. A candidate that failed to build is not one of these — another value of the same two classes may build.

status.description: `partial` where some rows were not read at all: a combination none of the rows seen reaches has not been left untried by anybody.

reason.description: Why there are no numbers, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. How large the space is says nothing about a behavior no row names.

notDerivable.description: Positions the model draws no line through. Not a gap — a statement that there was nothing to measure.

omitted.description: Positions dropped for being past the axis limit.

signature.description: What the rows establish about the cases of the behavior's inputs and its output. Absent where the behavior has no signature to read.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`.

specified.description: Cases a row expects. Somebody wrote down that the model owes this answer.

observed.description: Cases the behavior was seen to answer with, including from a row that expected something else.

verified.description: Cases a row expected and the behavior produced.

unclassifiedRows.description: Rows whose case could not be read. Above zero, a missing case is undecided rather than missing.

inputs.description: One entry per parameter, in order. A parameter that is not a sum has nothing to cover and reports empty sets.

executed.description: Cases the behavior was applied to. Not `observed`: nothing is claimed about what came back.

excluded.description: Cases the body answers `unreachable` for. Declared and not coverable: a row naming one would reach the `unreachable` and be refused, so they are counted out of what the rows are held to.

caseNames.description: Case names, sorted, so that two runs of the same model compare.

scope.description: What `subject` names, and so what the reason counts against. Anything larger than a behavior counts against every behavior inside it.

at.description: Where in which source. A position alone cannot say which file, since a module's rows are written across its own source and any attached ones.
